title: Cardiovascular Comprehensive Set 1: Cardiac Cycle (Short answer)

questions.prompt: Which electrical event on the ECG immediately precedes the mechanical event of atrial systole?
questions.modelAnswer: The P wave.

questions.prompt: What are the five criteria used to define "Normal Sinus Rhythm"?
questions.modelAnswer: (1) Normal P wave; (2) PR intervals between 0.12-0.2 s at constant interval; (3) Each P wave is always followed by a QRS complex; (4) QRS complexes duration less than 0.12 s; (5) Regular heart rate between 60-100 bpm

questions.prompt: What are the two primary phases of the ventricular cardiac cycle, and what do they represent?
questions.modelAnswer: Systole (ventricular contraction and ejection) and Diastole (ventricular relaxation and filling).

questions.prompt: At what specific point in the cardiac cycle does the first heart sound (S1) occur?
questions.modelAnswer: At the beginning of ventricular systole, immediately following the closure of the AV valves.

questions.prompt: Which mechanical event is responsible for the generation of the second heart sound (S2)?
questions.modelAnswer: The closure of the semilunar (aortic and pulmonic) valves at the beginning of ventricular relaxation.

questions.prompt: Describe the state of the cardiac valves during the isovolumetric contraction phase.
questions.modelAnswer: All valves (AV and semilunar) are closed, allowing pressure to rise without a change in volume.

questions.prompt: What occurs during the rapid ventricular ejection phase once ventricular pressure exceeds aortic pressure?
questions.modelAnswer: The aortic valve opens and blood is forcefully propelled into the aorta, rapidly decreasing ventricular volume.

questions.prompt: Why does aortic pressure begin to decrease during the phase of reduced ventricular ejection?
questions.modelAnswer: Aortic pressure falls because the rate of blood "running off" into the arterial tree exceeds the rate of blood being ejected from the ventricle.

questions.prompt: Define "isovolumetric relaxation" in terms of valve position and ventricular volume.
questions.modelAnswer: It is the period where the ventricle is relaxed and all valves are closed, resulting in a precipitous drop in pressure at a constant (minimum) volume.

questions.prompt: What pressure change triggers the opening of the mitral valve to begin the rapid ventricular filling phase?
questions.modelAnswer: The ventricular pressure falls below the left atrial pressure.

questions.prompt: Which phase of the cardiac cycle is the longest, and how is it affected by an increase in heart rate?
questions.modelAnswer: Reduced ventricular filling (diastasis); it is significantly shortened as heart rate increases, which can compromise filling.

questions.prompt: Under what physiological or clinical conditions is a third heart sound (S3) typically heard?
questions.modelAnswer: It is normal in children but indicates volume overload (e.g., heart failure) in adults.

questions.prompt: What is the origin of the fourth heart sound (S4), and why is it usually not audible in normal adults?
questions.modelAnswer: It is caused by atrial contraction filling a stiffened or non-compliant ventricle; it is usually inaudible in healthy adults due to high ventricular compliance.

questions.prompt: What does the "a" wave on a jugular venous pulse represent?
questions.modelAnswer: Atrial contraction.

questions.prompt: What mechanical event corresponds to the "c" wave observed in a jugular venous pulse?
questions.modelAnswer: Right ventricular contraction causing the tricuspid valve to bulge into the right atrium.

questions.prompt: Describe the physiological cause of the "v" wave in the jugular venous pulse.
questions.modelAnswer: Atrial filling occurring against a closed tricuspid valve during ventricular systole.

questions.prompt: What is the "dicrotic notch" (incisura) and what specific event produces it?
questions.modelAnswer: A small "blip" in the aortic pressure curve caused by the closure of the aortic valve.

questions.prompt: What is the primary determinant of pulse pressure in a healthy individual?
questions.modelAnswer: Stroke volume.

questions.prompt: State the formula for Ejection Fraction and its approximate normal value in a resting adult.
questions.modelAnswer: Ejection Fraction = Stroke Volume / End-Diastolic Volume; normal is approximately 0.55 (55%).

questions.prompt: In terms of ventricular volume, how is "preload" defined?
questions.modelAnswer: Left ventricular end-diastolic volume.

questions.prompt: In terms of pressure, how is "afterload" defined for the left ventricle?
questions.modelAnswer: Aortic pressure.

questions.prompt: Which segment of the ventricular pressure-volume loop represents isovolumetric contraction?
questions.modelAnswer: The segment where pressure increases vertically while volume remains at the end-diastolic value.

questions.prompt: On a pressure-volume loop, what mechanical phase is represented by the segment where volume decreases while pressure remains high?
questions.modelAnswer: Ventricular ejection.

questions.prompt: Which segment of the pressure-volume loop represents isovolumetric relaxation?
questions.modelAnswer: The segment where pressure decreases vertically while volume remains at the end-systolic value.

questions.prompt: Describe the segment of the pressure-volume loop that corresponds to ventricular filling.
questions.modelAnswer: The segment where volume increases at a relatively low and constant pressure.

questions.prompt: How does a sudden increase in afterload (e.g., increased aortic pressure) affect stroke volume and end-systolic volume?
questions.modelAnswer: It decreases stroke volume and increases end-systolic volume.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of increased myocardial contractility (positive inotropism) on the end-systolic volume and ejection fraction?
questions.modelAnswer: It decreases end-systolic volume and increases ejection fraction.

questions.prompt: According to the Frank-Starling Law, what is the effect of an increase in preload on the resulting stroke volume?
questions.modelAnswer: It increases stroke volume.

questions.prompt: What clinical measurement is used to estimate left atrial pressure?
questions.modelAnswer: Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.

questions.prompt: Explain why the second heart sound splits during inspiration.
questions.modelAnswer: Inspiration decreases intrathoracic pressure, increasing venous return to the right heart, which prolongs right ventricular ejection time and delays the closure of the pulmonic valve.
